novelty.readme_security: NOT acknowledged. README.md:340 enumerates the hook's acknowledged bypass classes as exactly three: a standalone script file, an interpreter one-liner (`python -c ...`), and a variable-built command. README.md:338 lists the wrappers the hook DOES peel as examples ('behind `timeout`, `nohup`, `env` or `uv run`') -- a non-exhaustive 'like' list, not an acknowledgement that an unlisted prefix wrapper silently suppresses the ask. 'Prefix the command with ionice/taskset/chrt/setarch' (or run it under pipenv/pdm/rye) is in none of the enumerated classes. The general 'the hook is attention, not the boundary' caveat (README.md:340,401) is a property of the whole mechanism, not an acknowledgement of this specific no-ask; reading it as blanket acknowledgement would make CHARTER §4 HOOK BYPASS a null win condition and the entire V8 hook work a fix of non-findings, which is incoherent.
novelty.v1_v8: NOT a fixed V1-V8 issue. V8 (the 10 hook bypasses, commit 2931038 'Fix the confirmed red-team findings') extended the command_words/nested_script logic for: uv/poetry VALUE-options (RUNNER_VALUE_OPTS), `env -S`/`--split-string` (env_split_string), value-taking shell options before `-c`, `eval` leading `--`, the MAX_NESTING fallback, ENVH_SESSION handling, and `--socket` before the subcommand. It added NO new wrapper/runner NAMES: WRAPPERS (envh_ask.py:36-47 = command/env/exec/nice/nohup/setsid/stdbuf/time/timeout/xargs) and RUNNERS (envh_ask.py:48 = {uv,poetry}) are unchanged. tests/test_hook.py asserts only in-table wrappers (nice, stdbuf, timeout, nohup, env -i, xargs, uv run, poetry run); there is NO regression test covering ionice/taskset/chrt/setarch/pipenv/pdm/rye. So this is a NEW, un-fixed gap in the same function, not a re-derivation of a fixed V8 issue and not a bypass of a V8 fix.
novelty.world: The technique (prefixing a trusted utility / project runner to proxy-execute a command past a name-based guard) is publicly known: ATT&CK T1127 (Trusted Developer Utilities Proxy Execution), T1202 (Indirect Command Execution), T1027 (Obfuscated Files or Information). Project-novel but a known technique class, reported as such per CHARTER §5 world-novelty clause.
novelty.judgment_known_vs_confirmed: Weighed the skeptical KNOWN reading (task flagged: 'same shape as the already-fixed V8 runner-table work ... expected incompleteness of a best-effort allow-list'). It does NOT demote to KNOWN under the charter's precise test: the specific wrappers/runners are neither in README's enumerated bypass classes nor marked fixed by any V1-V8 regression test. It is CONFIRMED but sits at the LOW end of novelty (same code path as V8; the enumerated allow-list is inherently incomplete), hence MEDIUM severity exactly per §6's 'hook bypass -> MEDIUM' mapping and the hard cap, with no escalation.

charter_clauses: §2 (operated only as rt1 via sudo -u; never root)
§3 (in scope: running the hook as rt1 is client-side userspace, explicitly in scope; not root-flavored)
§4 HOOK BYPASS (win condition: a command that starts an envh passphrase-requiring request while envh_ask.py returns no-ask, BEYOND README classes and V8 fixes)
§5 (NOVEL: not in README/SECURITY enumerated hook classes; not a fixed V1-V8 issue; project-novel known technique)
§6 (CONFIRMED; severity MEDIUM = hook bypass, hard-capped, hook is not a boundary)
reasoning: ROOT CAUSE: claude/hooks/envh_ask.py:425-454 command_words() peels only leading tokens whose basename is in WRAPPERS (lines 36-47) or in RUNNERS followed by `run` (line 48); for any other leading token it hits `else: break` (lines 445-446) and returns the words unchanged. decide() (line 527) then only enters the envh branch when posixpath.basename(name_and_arguments[0]) == 'envh'. For `ionice -c3 envh run ...` the surviving name is 'ionice' (and for `pipenv run envh ...' it is 'pipenv'), so basename != 'envh', the request is never examined, and the hook prints nothing. The WRAPPERS and RUNNERS sets are closed enumerations that omit the common util-linux prefix wrappers ionice/taskset/chrt/setarch and the project runners pipenv/pdm/rye (direct analogues of the handled uv/poetry). WHY CONFIRMED: I reproduced it as rt1 (non-root) with pasted output on a fresh instance (environment_id 578bbd3396c53a5c): the hook returns no-ask for all seven, while ionice/taskset/setarch/chrt(-o 0) end-to-end each reached a real passphrase-requiring broker request (#2-#5) that blocked with no approver; in-table controls (nice/stdbuf/uv run) and plain envh correctly ask. It is in scope (§3/§4 HOOK BYPASS), has the (capped) hook-bypass impact -- the in-app heads-up/deny-chance is suppressed while the console remains the boundary (all requests blocked) -- and is NOVEL (§5): not among README's three enumerated hook bypass classes and not covered or regression-fixed by V8, which changed no wrapper/runner names. SEVERITY MEDIUM strictly per §6's hook-bypass mapping and the hard cap; no secret was obtained and none was attempted; low novelty (same code path as V8, inherently-incomplete allow-list). CORRECTION to candidate: its pasted `chrt -f 99` form fails for a non-root user (CAP_SYS_NICE); the chrt gap is reachable via `chrt -o 0` instead. pipenv/pdm/rye are hook-level + code-inspection only (not installed), matching the attacker's own caveat.
recommended_fix: Make command_words()/decide() fail-closed on an unrecognized leading token (also scan the remaining words for a trailing `envh <session start|preset propose|import|run>` / fall back to PASSPHRASE_FORM) instead of silently `break`-ing; minimally, add ionice/taskset/chrt/setarch to WRAPPERS and pipenv/pdm/rye to RUNNERS -- but the enumerated allow-list is inherently incomplete, so the honest durable mitigation is that the hook is attention, not the boundary.
